questions.question: Which language should the Ingestion API use?
questions.rationale: Python and FastAPI were explicitly requested.

questions.question: Which framework should the Ingestion API use?

options.label: FastAPI
options.description: Explicitly requested for the ingestion service.

questions.question: What should the Ingestion API support?
questions.answer: Accept network security events, validate and normalize envelopes, publish durably to RabbitMQ, and expose health and readiness endpoints.
questions.rationale: These responsibilities follow from the requested Network Data → Ingestion API → RabbitMQ pipeline.
questions.recommendedChoice: Accept network security events, validate and normalize envelopes, publish durably to RabbitMQ, and expose health and readiness endpoints.

questions.question: Which language should the asynchronous security workers use?
questions.rationale: Python and Celery were explicitly requested.

options.label: Python
options.description: Matches the requested Celery worker stack.

questions.question: Which worker framework should the asynchronous pipeline use?
What should the asynchronous security workers do?
questions.answer: Parse and enrich events; run deterministic detection and correlation; calculate risk; invoke AI only for investigation summaries and analyst assistance; manage incident lifecycle; use retries and dead-letter queues.
questions.rationale: This preserves the requested pipeline and separates deterministic controls from AI.
questions.recommendedChoice: Parse and enrich events; run deterministic detection and correlation; calculate risk; invoke AI only for investigation summaries and analyst assistance; manage incident lifecycle; use retries and dead-letter queues.

questions.question: Which persistence and messaging services should the project use?
questions.rationale: PostgreSQL, RabbitMQ, and Redis were explicitly requested; no file/object storage is implied.

options.label: PostgreSQL
options.description: Incident records, event metadata, and durable operational state.

options.label: RabbitMQ
options.description: Requested event queue, retries, and dead-letter routing.

options.label: Redis
options.description: Requested cache and Celery broker/result support where appropriate.

options.label: No datastore required
options.description: Choose only when no persistence, messaging, storage, or cache is needed.

questions.question: Will users sign in to access application API features?
questions.rationale: The described scope is a backend ingestion and processing pipeline with no user-facing API workflow. Service-to-service authentication remains a deployment/security design decision, not user sign-in.

options.label: Yes
options.description: Users authenticate to access application API features.

options.label: No
options.description: No user sign-in flow is in scope.
